## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 8.87 at N=10000 (above L1d spill at N≈963, within L2) to 7.67 at N=100000 (past L2 spill at N≈61680), then stays flat at ~8.0 through N=10000000. The small-N premium is overhead amortization, not a cache effect. There is no knee at the L2→DRAM spill — cost is flat from N=100000 onward. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: q=0.1 holds ~9.2, q=0.25 holds ~11.2, q=0.5 holds ~13.7 ns/p, all flat across N. The L1d spill at N≈963 is below the smallest measured N, so its effect is not directly visible.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.87 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — 29.7% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. The algo is compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: at q=0.01, N=100000, the profile shows compute=64.3% and backend_stall=30.5%. Bandwidth stays flat at ~8.5 GB/s from N=100000 through N=10000000, never rising toward the ceiling as N grows. Death rate drives monotonic collapse: 8.87→7.83→6.47→5.25 GB/s (best per q) as branch_flush rises from 4.0% to 35.5%, transitioning the bottleneck from compute to branches by q=0.5.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. The update loop loads a single particle via `ldr q7, [x10]` (4 floats), `ldr d16, [x10, #0x10]` (2 floats), and `ldr s6, [x10, #0xc]`, then uses `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` and `mov.s v17[3], v6[0]` to pack components into a 4-lane vector for `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s`. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x11]` loads a single element into lane 1. Stride is 0x44=68 bytes, matching bytes_per_particle. The scatter phase uses byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` pairs for RGB pixel writes. Component-wise vec on stride-68 with byte-scatter stores explains the 30% ceiling fraction — there is no cross-particle SIMD to amortize per-particle load/store overhead.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo sustains 8.87 GB/s = 29.7% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling with no cache-spill knee and no bandwidth growth with N, because component-wise vectorization within a single 68-byte particle cannot stream. The profile confirms compute-bound operation (64.3% compute at N=100000), and death rate collapses throughput to 5.25 GB/s by q=0.5 as branch_flush reaches 35.5%.
